title: What Criminology Studies — Fundamentals of Criminology
description: Signature edition. This entry teaches What Criminology Studies as part of the fundamentals of criminology, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Foundations tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of criminology, What Criminology Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Defining crime means the social construction of which harms become crimes. Social learning means crime learned like any behavior, through associations. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Defining crime: the social construction of which harms become crimes.
Social learning: crime learned like any behavior, through associations.
key_laws: Deterrence: certainty of punishment deterring more than severity.
vocabulary: Recidivism: reoffending after punishment or release.
Hot spots: the small places producing most crime.
methods: Crime statistics: reading UCR, victimization surveys, and self-reports critically.
history: Criminology began with Beccaria's 1764 On Crimes and Punishments; Lombroso's biological theories and the Chicago school's sociology followed. Postwar theory exploded, and evidence-based policy now tests what actually reduces crime.
